newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. plans $151 mln school funding boost.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. plans $151 mln school funding boost.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson said Tuesday he would seek to provide $151 million in the state's 1997-1998 budget to help fund public school class-size reduction.

Wilson said in a statement that he would earmark in his 1997-1998 budget $141 million in surplus operational funds and propose to allocate $10 million in one-time monies for class-size reduction programs.
"I plan to submit urgency legislation to speed up class-size reduction for every school in California that's requested it," Wilson, a Republican, said.
"I proposed we shift that money right away to meet facility needs," Wilson said.
Wilson's 1996-1997 budget provided $771 million in ongoing operational funding and $200 million in facilities funding to reduce class sizes.
Legislation to enable both the redirection of the $141 million and the allocation of the $10 million will be introduced in January of 1997 by Assemblyman Curt Pringle.
To date, 95 percent of California elementary and unified school districts are participating in Wilson's class size reduction program, Wilson said.
